review: 608.1-1: the pass order in the decisions and the response delta was wrong (the caster of a response receives priority first); restated it as A passes, B casts and passes, A passes.
608.2a-1: never-triggers was labelled does_not_fire, but there the trigger is never put on the stack (603.4), so 608.2a never applies; relabelled it other.
608.2h-1: target-leaves was labelled does_not_fire, but it is a 608.2b fizzle in which 608.2h never applies; relabelled it other and noted in forge_notes that 608.2h has no does_not_fire branch.

608.2j-2: was a Doom Blade targeting-legality check (601.2c/115, not an effect, so not 608.2j); rewrote it as a Hellfire resolution, the rule's own 'destroy all nonblack creatures' case, with Edgewalker spared versus Grizzly Bears destroyed.

608.2k: the skip claimed only exotic cards reach it and that it adds nothing beyond 608.2h; both false (a Theros god losing devotion while blocked by Wall of Tears is the rule's own example). Removed the skip and added 608.2k-1.

608.2p: the skip claimed Forge has no 'when an ability resolves' trigger; Forge has Mode$ AbilityResolves (Narci, Fable Singer; Tom Bombadil; Tyvar the Bellicose). Removed the skip and added 608.2p-1 with Narci and History of Benalia.

skipped.reason: cannot be illustrated with a simple Forge state: it needs a resolving instant, sorcery or ability that leaves the stack part-way through its own resolution, which no basic card does; ordinary resolution to the graveyard is covered by 608.2n-1

scenarios.title: The top object of the stack resolves each time both players pass in succession
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping one Mountain.
A passes priority, then B passes priority; Shock resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: After both players pass once, A's Shock resolves: Grizzly Bears (2/2) takes 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard; Shock moves to A's graveyard; the stack is empty.

variants.label: response
variants.delta: After A passes with Shock on the stack, B responds by casting Shock targeting A, tapping B's Mountain; B passes, then A passes.
variants.expected: After both players pass once, only B's Shock (the top object) resolves: A's life is 18, B's Shock is in B's graveyard. A's Shock is still on the stack and Grizzly Bears has no damage; A's Shock resolves only after a second round of passes.

scenarios.title: An intervening-if trigger whose condition is false on resolution does nothing

setup.notes: A's upkeep begins; Felidar Sovereign's trigger (if you have 40 or more life, you win the game) goes on the stack.

decisions: The upkeep trigger is put on the stack (A has 40 life, so the condition is true when it triggers).
A passes priority; B passes priority; the trigger resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The trigger resolves with A at 40 life: A wins the game.

variants.label: life-lost-in-response
variants.delta: B responds by casting Shock targeting A, tapping Mountain, before the trigger resolves.
variants.expected: A's life is 38 when the trigger would resolve; the condition is false, the trigger is removed from the stack and does nothing; nobody wins and the game continues.

variants.label: never-triggers
variants.delta: A starts at 39 life instead of 40 and B casts nothing.
variants.expected: The trigger does not go on the stack at all; nobody wins.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge expresses the condition as trigger parameters (LifeTotal / LifeAmount); check that Forge re-evaluates it on resolution and does not only check it when the trigger is put on the stack.

scenarios.title: A spell whose only target became illegal does not resolve at all
decisions: A casts Sorin's Thirst targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping both Swamps.
B passes priority; A passes priority; Sorin's Thirst resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The target is still legal: Sorin's Thirst resolves, Grizzly Bears takes 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard, and A gains 2 life (A at 22).

variants.label: target-leaves
variants.delta: B responds by casting Unsummon on Grizzly Bears, tapping Island; Unsummon resolves first.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is in B's hand, so Sorin's Thirst has no legal target: it does not resolve, moves to A's graveyard, and A gains no life (A stays at 20).

scenarios.title: A spell with some legal targets resolves and skips only the illegal ones

setup.notes: Llanowar Elves is summoning sick and not used for mana.

decisions: A casts Arc Trail, choosing Grizzly Bears for 2 damage and Llanowar Elves for 1 damage, tapping both Mountains.
B passes priority; A passes priority; Arc Trail resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Both targets are legal: Grizzly Bears takes 2 damage and Llanowar Elves takes 1 damage; both move to B's graveyard.

variants.label: one-target-leaves
variants.delta: B responds by casting Unsummon on Llanowar Elves, tapping one Island; Unsummon resolves first.
variants.expected: Llanowar Elves is in B's hand. Arc Trail still resolves for its remaining legal target: Grizzly Bears takes 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard; the Elves are unaffected; Arc Trail moves to A's graveyard.

variants.label: both-targets-leave
variants.delta: B responds with both Unsummons, one on each creature, tapping both Islands; both resolve first.
variants.expected: Both creatures are in B's hand. Arc Trail has no legal target: it does not resolve and moves to A's graveyard; no damage is dealt.

scenarios.title: A legal target that fails a resolution-time condition resolves and does nothing
decisions: A casts Pyroblast choosing the mode 'Destroy target permanent if it's blue', targeting Merfolk of the Pearl Trident, tapping Mountain.
B passes priority; A passes priority; Pyroblast resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The target is legal and blue: Pyroblast resolves and Merfolk of the Pearl Trident is destroyed (B's graveyard); Pyroblast moves to A's graveyard.

variants.label: not-blue
variants.delta: B's creature is Grizzly Bears (green) instead of Merfolk of the Pearl Trident, and A targets it.
variants.expected: Pyroblast resolves (it is not countered or fizzled) but does nothing: Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield undamaged; Pyroblast moves to A's graveyard.

variants.label: target-leaves
variants.delta: B responds by casting Unsummon on Merfolk of the Pearl Trident, tapping Island.
variants.expected: Merfolk is in B's hand; Pyroblast's target is illegal, so it fizzles (does not resolve) and moves to A's graveyard.

scenarios.forge_notes: The not-blue variant needs Grizzly Bears in place of Merfolk on B's battlefield; Island and Unsummon are unused there.

scenarios.title: Later text modifies earlier text: destroy, and it can't be regenerated
decisions: A casts Terror targeting River Boa, tapping both Swamps.
B activates River Boa's regenerate ability ({G}), tapping Forest, creating a regeneration shield; the ability resolves.
Both players pass; Terror resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Terror destroys River Boa and the regeneration shield cannot save it: River Boa moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: no-clause
variants.delta: A casts Doom Blade (no regeneration clause) instead of Terror.
variants.expected: Doom Blade destroys River Boa but the regeneration shield replaces it: River Boa stays on the battlefield, tapped, with no damage and the shield used up.

scenarios.title: An effect acting on several objects processes them simultaneously
decisions: A casts Day of Judgment, tapping all four Plains.
Both players pass; Day of Judgment resolves.
For each Blood Artist trigger that goes on the stack, A targets B.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Blood Artist and Grizzly Bears are destroyed simultaneously, so Blood Artist sees both deaths: two triggers fire, B loses 2 life (B at 18) and A gains 2 life (A at 22).

variants.label: one-at-a-time
variants.delta: A has two Mountains and two Shocks instead of the Plains and Day of Judgment; A casts one Shock on Blood Artist, then after it resolves a second Shock on Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Blood Artist dies first and triggers once (B at 19, A at 21); when Grizzly Bears dies afterwards, Blood Artist is gone and does not trigger. One trigger fired in total.

scenarios.forge_notes: The one-at-a-time variant replaces A's lands and hand: Mountain, Mountain on the battlefield and Shock, Shock in hand.

scenarios.title: A spell cast during resolution goes on top of the stack and resolves before the casting source

setup.notes: A's library top card is Lightning Bolt.

decisions: A casts Bloodbraid Elf, tapping all four lands; the cascade trigger goes on the stack above it.
Both players pass; the cascade trigger resolves: Lightning Bolt is exiled and A chooses to cast it without paying, targeting Grizzly Bears.
Both players pass; Lightning Bolt resolves; both players pass again; Bloodbraid Elf resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Lightning Bolt is cast without priority passing and goes on top of the stack, so it resolves before Bloodbraid Elf: Grizzly Bears dies, Bolt goes to A's graveyard, and then Bloodbraid Elf enters A's battlefield. The cascade trigger has left the stack.

variants.label: nothing-cheaper
variants.delta: A's library is Serra Angel, then Mountain; no nonland card with lesser mana value exists.
variants.expected: No spell is cast: Serra Angel and Mountain are put on the bottom of A's library; Grizzly Bears has no damage; Bloodbraid Elf resolves and enters A's battlefield.

scenarios.title: An effect that needs information about a departed object uses its last known information
decisions: A casts Swords to Plowshares targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Plains.
B passes priority; A passes priority; Swords to Plowshares resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is exiled and B gains life equal to its last known power, 2: B is at 22.

variants.label: pumped
variants.delta: B responds by casting Giant Growth on Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest; Giant Growth resolves first.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a 5/5 when exiled, so its last known power is 5: Grizzly Bears is exiled and B gains 5 life (B at 25).

variants.label: target-leaves
variants.delta: B responds by casting Unsummon on Grizzly Bears, tapping Island.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is in B's hand; Swords to Plowshares fizzles, B gains no life (B at 20).

scenarios.forge_notes: 608.2h has no does_not_fire branch: last known information is always used once the object has left. The target-leaves variant is a 608.2b fizzle kept as a contrast where no information is needed at all.

scenarios.title: An effect that looks back in time counts an attack by a creature that no longer exists

setup.notes: Grizzly Bears is not summoning sick.

decisions: A attacks with Grizzly Bears only.
B blocks Grizzly Bears with Centaur Courser.
Combat damage: Grizzly Bears deals 2 to Centaur Courser and Centaur Courser deals 3 to Grizzly Bears.
In main phase 2, A casts Mardu Heart-Piercer, tapping all four Mountains; it resolves.
If Heart-Piercer's raid trigger goes on the stack, A targets B; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears died in combat and is in A's graveyard, but A attacked this turn: Heart-Piercer's raid trigger fires and deals 2 damage to B (B at 18).

variants.label: no-attack
variants.delta: A does not attack with Grizzly Bears; combat is skipped.
variants.expected: A did not attack this turn: Heart-Piercer enters, its raid trigger does not fire, and B stays at 20; Grizzly Bears is still on the battlefield.

scenarios.title: An effect referring to a color checks only that color
decisions: A casts Cleanse, tapping all four Plains.
Both players pass; Cleanse resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Edgewalker is black (and white), so 'destroy all black creatures' destroys it: Edgewalker moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: green-creature
variants.delta: B's creature is Grizzly Bears instead of Edgewalker.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is not black: it stays on the battlefield undamaged; Cleanse moves to A's graveyard.

scenarios.title: 'Destroy all nonblack creatures' spares a white-and-black creature
decisions: A casts Hellfire, tapping all five Swamps.
Both players pass; Hellfire resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Edgewalker is black, so it is not a nonblack creature: it stays on the battlefield. No creature died, so Hellfire deals 3 damage to A (A at 17); Hellfire moves to A's graveyard.

variants.label: green-creature
variants.delta: B's creature is Grizzly Bears instead of Edgewalker.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is nonblack: it is destroyed and moves to B's graveyard. One creature died, so Hellfire deals 4 damage to A (A at 16).

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge counts X from the cards Hellfire destroyed (RememberDestroyed).

scenarios.title: A trigger still returns the creature it referred to after that permanent stops being a creature

setup.notes: A's devotion to white is 5 (Heliod 1, each Serra Angel 2), so Heliod is a 5/6 indestructible creature.

decisions: A attacks with Heliod, God of the Sun only.
B blocks Heliod with Wall of Tears; Wall of Tears' trigger resolves, setting up the return at end of combat.
Still in the declare blockers step, B casts Doom Blade targeting one Serra Angel, tapping both Swamps; it resolves.
Both players pass through combat damage to the end of combat step; the delayed trigger resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: One Serra Angel is in A's graveyard; A's devotion to white drops to 3, so Heliod stops being a creature and leaves combat; no combat damage is dealt. At end of combat Heliod, now a noncreature enchantment, is still returned to A's hand.

variants.label: still-creature
variants.delta: B does not cast Doom Blade.
variants.expected: Heliod stays a 5/6 creature and deals 5 damage to Wall of Tears, which moves to B's graveyard; at end of combat Heliod is returned to A's hand.

scenarios.forge_notes: 608.2k has no does_not_fire branch: the referred object is affected whatever characteristics it gained or lost. Forge remembers the blocked creature as an LKI copy (TriggeredAttackerLKICopy); check that the bounce still finds Heliod once it is no longer a creature.

scenarios.title: A resolved spell goes to the graveyard and a resolved ability ceases to exist
decisions: A casts Firebolt from hand targeting B, tapping one Mountain.
Both players pass; Firebolt resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: B takes 2 damage (B at 18) and Firebolt moves from the stack to A's graveyard.

variants.label: flashback
variants.delta: Firebolt starts in A's graveyard instead of A's hand, and A casts it with flashback ({4}{R}), tapping all five Mountains.
variants.expected: B takes 2 damage (B at 18) and Firebolt is exiled instead of going to A's graveyard.

variants.label: ability
variants.delta: The object is not a spell: A has an untapped Prodigal Sorcerer (instead of Firebolt) and activates it targeting B.
variants.expected: B takes 1 damage (B at 19); the ability is removed from the stack and ceases to exist; Prodigal Sorcerer stays on the battlefield, tapped, and nothing goes to a graveyard.

scenarios.forge_notes: The ability variant adds Prodigal Sorcerer (not summoning sick) to A's battlefield and removes Firebolt from the hand.

scenarios.title: An ability that triggers when another ability resolves triggers after that resolution

setup.notes: A's precombat main phase has just begun: the turn-based action adds a lore counter to History of Benalia and the chapter ability for that counter goes on the stack. A controls no Knights.

decisions: Both players pass; the chapter ability resolves.
If two triggers of Narci, Fable Singer go on the stack together, A puts the life-drain trigger on top; both players pass on each and they resolve.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Chapter III (the final chapter) resolves; Narci's trigger fires: B loses 3 life (B at 17) and A gains 3 life (A at 23). History of Benalia is sacrificed by the state-based check and moves to A's graveyard; Narci's sacrifice trigger fires and A draws Plains.

variants.label: not-final-chapter
variants.delta: History of Benalia starts with 1 lore counter instead of 2.
variants.expected: Chapter II resolves: A creates a 2/2 white Knight token with vigilance. Narci's trigger does not fire; life totals stay 20 and 20; History of Benalia stays on the battlefield with 2 lore counters; A draws nothing.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge implements the trigger as Mode$ AbilityResolves with ValidSpellAbility$ Triggered.LastChapter.

scenarios.title: A permanent spell without targets enters the battlefield under its controller's control
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests.
B passes priority; A passes priority; Grizzly Bears resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears becomes a permanent and enters the battlefield under A's control.

variants.label: countered
variants.delta: B responds with Counterspell, tapping both Islands.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears never resolves: it is countered and moves to A's graveyard; nothing enters A's battlefield.

scenarios.title: An Aura spell enters attached to its target, or goes to the graveyard if the target is illegal
decisions: A casts Pacifism targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping both Plains.
B passes priority; A passes priority; Pacifism resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Pacifism enters the battlefield under A's control attached to Grizzly Bears; Grizzly Bears can't attack or block.

variants.label: target-leaves
variants.delta: B responds by casting Unsummon on Grizzly Bears, tapping Island.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is in B's hand; Pacifism has an illegal target, does not resolve and is put into A's graveyard; it never enters the battlefield.

scenarios.title: A bestowed Aura spell with an illegal target resolves as a creature spell
decisions: A casts Hopeful Eidolon for its bestow cost ({3}{W}) targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping all four Plains.
B passes priority; A passes priority; the spell resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The target is legal: Hopeful Eidolon enters attached to Grizzly Bears as an Aura; Grizzly Bears is a 3/3 with lifelink and Hopeful Eidolon is not a creature.

variants.label: target-leaves
variants.delta: B responds by casting Unsummon on A's Grizzly Bears, tapping Island.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is in A's hand. The bestowed spell does not fizzle: it becomes a creature spell and resolves, so Hopeful Eidolon enters A's battlefield as a 1/1 lifelink creature (not in the graveyard).

scenarios.title: A mutating creature spell merges with its target, or enters alone if the target is illegal

setup.notes: B controls no artifact or enchantment, so Gemrazer's mutate trigger has no target.

decisions: A casts Gemrazer for its mutate cost ({1}{G}{G}) targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping all three Forests; A will put it over the target.
B passes priority; A passes priority; the spell resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Gemrazer merges with Grizzly Bears: A controls one creature permanent that is a 4/4 Gemrazer with reach and trample; Grizzly Bears is part of it, not a separate permanent.

variants.label: target-leaves
variants.delta: B responds by casting Unsummon on A's Grizzly Bears, tapping Island.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is in A's hand. The mutating spell resolves as a creature spell: Gemrazer enters A's battlefield as an ordinary 4/4 with reach and trample; nothing merged.

scenarios.forge_notes: Mutate onto a creature then bouncing the target in response may be hard to reach in Forge's puzzle mode; use an interventional fork if needed.

scenarios.title: A permanent spell that can't enter the battlefield is put into its owner's graveyard

setup.notes: Worms of the Earth: lands can't enter the battlefield.

decisions: A casts Clone, tapping all four Islands.
Both players pass; Clone resolves and A chooses to have it enter as a copy of Dryad Arbor.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: As a copy of Dryad Arbor Clone would be a land and can't enter the battlefield: Clone is put into A's graveyard.

variants.label: copy-bears
variants.delta: A chooses to have Clone enter as a copy of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: A copy of Grizzly Bears is not a land: Clone enters A's battlefield as a 2/2 Grizzly Bears copy.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's Clone replacement effect and Worms' replacement ('Lands can't enter the battlefield') may not combine as the rule describes; verify in the engine.

scenarios.title: A copy of a permanent spell becomes a token as it enters the battlefield
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping two Forests.
With Grizzly Bears on the stack, A activates Lithoform Engine ({4}, {T}) targeting that spell, tapping the other four Forests.
Both players pass; the copy resolves, then both players pass again and the original resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: A controls two Grizzly Bears: the original card and a token that is the copy.

variants.label: no-copy
variants.delta: A does not activate Lithoform Engine.
variants.expected: A controls one Grizzly Bears (the card) and no token.

scenarios.forge_notes: Only the token-ness of the copy is hard to see in current records (needs_new_fields).

scenarios.title: A delayed trigger from a static ability on the stack is created as the permanent enters
decisions: A casts Mardu Scout for its dash cost ({1}{R}), tapping both Mountains.
Both players pass; Mardu Scout resolves and enters the battlefield.
The turn advances to the beginning of the end step.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Mardu Scout enters with haste; at the beginning of the end step the delayed trigger returns it to A's hand.

variants.label: hard-cast
variants.delta: A casts Mardu Scout for its normal mana cost ({R}{R}) instead of dashing it.
variants.expected: No delayed trigger is created: Mardu Scout stays on A's battlefield at the end step.
